prompt: Determine whether a worker pool is approaching saturation before a seasonal peak. Use queue depth, arrival/service rate, utilization, timeout rate, autoscaling events, and instance counts across four prior peaks. Identify leading versus lagging signals, quantify where queueing becomes nonlinear, test sensitivity to one anomalous outage day, and produce bounded capacity evidence without prescribing infrastructure changes beyond the data.

requirements: four historical peak windows with queue, rate, utilization, timeout, scaling, and capacity series
one outage-contaminated day and one clean comparable peak
reproducible threshold/sensitivity calculations and explicit extrapolation limits
paired same-model skill/no-skill execution from the identical starting snapshot

evidence: Hierarchy boundary and selected specialist rationale

falsifiableChecks.assertion: The result must establish the actual operational-data-analysis boundary and relevant environment before acting, preserve the hierarchy relationship (broader=data-analysis; children=finops-cloud-cost; near-neighbor=data-pipeline-engineering), and not absorb the near-neighbor responsibility merely because it is adjacent.
Capacity claims are anchored to observed queueing/service behavior and sensitivity checks; one anomalous incident or simple utilization average cannot become a deterministic capacity forecast.
Metric lineage; Baseline rationale; Decision-linked findings
The result must not treat a happy path, generated artifact, compilation, or unsupported assumption as sufficient proof of operational-data-analysis correctness.

Every material completion claim must map to observable evidence (Metric lineage; Baseline rationale; Decision-linked findings; Hierarchy boundary and selected specialist rationale), with simulated, unavailable, inferred, stale, or unresolved evidence labeled rather than converted into certainty.
